title: The Messy Reality of Scale: Synthetic Data and Pre-Training — Marah Abdin & Robert McHardy, poolside
talk_summary: Poolside's data and pre-training leads describe how they scaled from Laguna M to XS/S: modular synthetic-data pipelines (seeds, generator, filters, orchestrators, supervisor) to fight repetition and expose implicit reasoning, plus aggressive invariant checks (weight-hash across replicas, FP32 accumulation, crash-on-mismatch) to catch silent corruption at scale. Most content is model-training specific, but the pipeline-modularity and invariant-checking patterns transfer to agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Modular pipeline decomposition with orchestrator + supervisor
takeaways.what_they_do: Every synthetic-data pipeline is composed of the same six parts (seeds, metadata, generator, filters/validators, orchestrator, supervisor); an orchestrator dynamically picks which agent runs next/skips and a supervisor polices it with a global view.

takeaways.technique: Break hard tasks into simpler sub-steps
takeaways.what_they_do: Rule of thumb: if a task is too hard for the model it loses correctness and diversity, so they decompose tasks (e.g. novel: setting/characters/plot first, then chapters) and use multi-stage workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if task is too hard for your model, then your model will start to fall on its face. Lose correctness, lose diversity. So break down the task, make it simpler.

takeaways.what_they_do: Compute a hash over model weights across replicas each interval; identical hashes mean continue, mismatch means crash training immediately because it should never happen.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if all of these hashes are identical, then we know we can continue training. If they're not identical... we crash the training.

takeaways.technique: Silent-corruption blind spots in redundant checks
takeaways.what_they_do: They note hash checks only work where replicas are redundant; race conditions in forward/backward are invisible because real runs have no duplicate to compare, so they plan a dry-run hash checker.
takeaways.evidence_quote: In real training runs, you don't have any redundancy... so you can never check if forward and backward actually behave the same
takeaways.numbers: ~0.5% of gradients silently corrupted by a race condition

takeaways.what_they_do: They built an 'auto mixer' to do cheaper sweeps on clusters of datasets before committing to expensive full experiments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we implemented auto mixer that basically just gives us a chance to do a cheaper sweep on clusters of our sets before moving on to more expensive experiments

takeaways.technique: Cheap seed-heavy pipelines vs expensive orchestrated ones
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly tier pipelines: cheap scalable ones with smaller models and heavy seeds (rephrasing) vs complex orchestrated ones reserved for high-value data (educational).
takeaways.numbers: 13% synthetic share of pre-training mix; 6T-token corpus
